Read the passage provided (Text A — a personal essay about a community garden).

How do the writer's language choices help us understand their feelings about growing food with others? You might consider how they have used:
• descriptions of the natural world
• ideas about shared effort and cooperation
• ideas about patience and reward.

Support your explanation with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Identify and describe aspects of the text that are relevant to the question; explain how one or more aspects create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together to build meaning across the text. Excellence: Explain how aspects have been deliberately chosen to create meanings and effects that connect to the writer's purpose and broader contexts. Look for: sensory imagery (sight, smell, touch of the garden); metaphor or personification applied to plants or seasons; contrast between solitary effort and communal gathering; sentence variation to mirror the rhythm of planting and harvesting; tone shifts from uncertainty to satisfaction.

Read the poem provided (Text B — a poem about walking home at dusk).

How does the poet help us understand the speaker's reflections on change? You might consider how they have used:
• imagery of light and darkness
• ideas about memory and the passage of time
• the mood or atmosphere of the poem.

Support your explanation with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Identify and describe aspects of the text that are relevant to the question; explain how one or more aspects create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together to build meaning across the text. Excellence: Explain how aspects have been deliberately chosen to create meanings and effects that connect to the writer's purpose and broader contexts. Look for: light/dark symbolism representing knowledge and uncertainty; use of past and present tense to show the speaker moving between memory and reality; repetition or refrain that echoes the cyclical nature of change; enjambment creating a sense of movement; contrast between familiar landmarks and unfamiliar feelings.

Read the passage provided (Text C — a narrative about a family preparing for a storm).

How does the writer help us understand the family's experience of facing an uncertain situation? You might consider how they have used:
• descriptions of actions and preparations
• ideas about roles within a family
• mood or atmosphere.

Support your explanation with quotes and examples of language features from the text.
questions.markingGuide: Achieved: Identify and describe aspects of the text that are relevant to the question; explain how one or more aspects create meaning. Merit: Explain how two or more aspects work together to build meaning across the text. Excellence: Explain how aspects have been deliberately chosen to create meanings and effects that connect to the writer's purpose and broader contexts. Look for: short, urgent sentences to build tension; listing of practical tasks to show how people cope through action; dialogue or lack of dialogue revealing family dynamics; personification of the storm or weather; contrast between the chaos outside and the routine inside; how different family members respond differently, revealing character and relationships.
